title: The Garden That Grew Past Its Sign
synopsis: Amy and Ben find the once-small garden tall with sunflower stalks; Grandma May explains the radish harvest, and Amy adds an in-between sketch to the existing folder.
continuity_state: Before: After the nine-season map extension, the garden has been tended by adults through many weeks. At 030000 the radishes were seedlings and two sunflower shoots had emerged; an early garden drawing is in the Story House folder. After: Two sunflower stems have grown tall; one has a round green bud and the other is shorter. The radishes were harvested by caretakers at their proper time in preceding weeks, some washed and eaten, leaving the front row empty with its red label. The sign is partly hidden by a leaf but has not yet moved. Amy puts a small interim tall-plant sketch into the original LITTLE GROWING GARDEN folder beside the first picture. Map remains unchanged.

related_resources.reason: University of Minnesota Extension places garden-radish harvest about three to five weeks after sowing; offstage harvest avoids keeping spring radishes in the ground for months.
The New York Botanical Garden describes the much longer course from sunflower seed to mature flowers; the change over many weeks is deliberately gradual.
